adjudication.rationale: The factual claim verifies exactly: `retention.complete` has one call site, `retain_accepted` (mcp-re-proxy/src/http_profile_serve/reply_assembly/accepted.rs:111-117), which is reached from only two places — `serve_retained` (accepted.rs:47) and `answer_notification`'s Ok arm (notification.rs:60) — so every post-crossing refusal (`assemble_reply`'s four arms at reply_assembly/mod.rs:98, 107, 111, 78; notification.rs:89; notification.rs:122) returns without discharging it. The out-of-packet question is answered half in the design's favour: an uncompleted `DispatchCommitted` is a RECOGNISED state, not an anomaly — the `.pending` marker means 'this request crossed the execution threshold and its outcome was never retained', it deliberately has no `Drop`, and over-reporting indeterminacy is stated as the safe direction (mcp-re-proxy/src/transparency/dispatch_committed.rs:21-36). What survives is a real evidence loss on a reachable path: with retention on, a backend reply with an unrecognized `resultType` yields a signed 502 at mcp-re-proxy/src/http_profile_serve/reply.rs:97, the client receives bytes the deployment then retains nothing about, and the module's own claim that a retention deployment 'can account for everything it served' (retention.rs:4-5) fails for that class. The marker left behind is also unreachable operationally: `pending_reservations()` (transparency/durability.rs:292-294) has zero production callers — its only caller is a test — so nothing enumerates or reaps them and they accumulate one file per forced refusal.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Route post-crossing refusals through the same discharge the success terminals use: the refusal response IS the served response, so `retain_accepted` (which already returns `Some(rejection)` on its own failure) should be called with it before the refusal is returned. That turns the `.pending` marker into a completed hop naming the actual outcome, and reserves genuine indeterminacy for the case it was designed for — a process that died mid-exchange.

adjudication.rationale: The interleaving is real. `guard`'s success path writes `*self.until.lock()... = None` unconditionally on the `Ok(_) if probing` arm (`handshake_quota.rs:166-170`), with no check that the `until` now in the cell is the one this thread installed at :158. A thread that entered while the cell was `None` (so `probing == false`) and whose signer call outlives the cooldown arms from a clock reading taken AFTER its call (:172 -> `arm`, :121-125); if that arm lands before a probing thread's success, the probe's clear destroys a window that a genuine `Exhausted` verdict opened at a LATER instant than the probe's own. That is the exact loss `arm`'s `current.max(until)` and its dedicated control `a_straggler_cannot_shorten_the_window` (:342) exist to prevent, taken to the limit. Every control in the file is single-threaded with an explicit clock, so nothing exercises two in-flight calls with different verdicts. Cost is bounded — one lost window is one cooldown (equal to the network timeout) of unthrottled handshake signing before the next `Exhausted` re-arms — so severity medium -> low.
adjudication.smallest_fix: In `HandshakeQuotaWindow::guard` (mcp-re-proxy/src/handshake_quota.rs), have the probing thread remember the `Instant` it installed at :158 and clear only when the cell still holds that value, so a success can never discard a window another thread's quota verdict armed; add a control that drives the two orderings against an explicit clock.

adjudication.rationale: Correct as read. `add_key` is the only mutator of the trust map in either verifier — `self.keys.retain(|entry| entry.key_id != key_id); self.keys.push(...)` (v1.rs:180-184, v2.rs:438-442) — and `permit_ingress_identity` (v2.rs:446-449) only inserts into a `BTreeSet`. There is no `remove_key`, no expiry, and no operation over the SET, so `retain` covers only rotation that REUSES a key id; minting `attestor-2` and retiring `attestor-1` leaves `attestor-1` trusted for the process lifetime. The doc comment is not the defect — v1.rs:177-179 claims exactly the narrower same-id property — the SHAPE is: trust is accumulated per-value rather than being a projection of the configured set. Unreachable today (Modes B and C refused at config_state/transport.rs:184-191 and 287-298), and in fact there is no production constructor for either verifier at all, so this is the deferred half's own change rule applying (ingress/mod.rs:23-25: the suite is the only thing keeping it correct, and a check is not weakened because nothing reaches it).
adjudication.smallest_fix: Take the trust material at construction rather than accumulating it: `LbAssertionBinding::new(source, keys)` and `LbAssertionV2Binding::new(source, audience, keys, ingress_identities)`, with the `Vec<LbKeyEntry>` / `BTreeSet<String>` private and no `&mut self` mutator. 'Trusted' then means 'in the configured set', rotation is a new verifier, and the clone-divergence reported as R11-682 closes in the same edit.

adjudication.rationale: Working as designed, with the decision and its cost both written down. `create_root` (private_file.rs:24-47) creates the root `0700` through `DirBuilder::mode`, then stats an EXISTING root and warns when `mode & 0o077 != 0`, naming what is in the directory ('live bearer tokens and DPoP proofs') and what to do ('Restrict it to 0700'). The decision not to tighten is argued at the point of the decision: 'silently tightening a path a sidecar or an auditor may share is not this module's call' (private_file.rs:32-34), and the deployment-facing doc states the same posture without overclaiming — 'an existing directory that is looser is warned about at startup' (transparency/mod.rs:81-84). The 'fails closed' posture this module does take is about writes it cannot make (transparency/mod.rs:29-41), which is a different fact from the custody of a directory the operator chose. Nothing here claims the store is enforced 0700, so there is no claim to narrow either.

adjudication.rationale: The premise that makes this a defect — that an exchange can outlive its snapshot's `exp` and still sign under it — does not hold, because `now` is fixed for the whole exchange and is never re-read. `Exchange::now` is set once in `handle` (http_profile_serve/mod.rs:459-465) and documented as fixed at mod.rs:158-161 and 168-174. The snapshot on the exchange is produced ONLY by `answerable_stage` via `self.responses.window(ex.now)` -> `SigningWindow::open(&self.signer, now, ...)` -> `signer.current(now)`, which is exactly where `now < exp` is enforced (answering_commitment.rs:73-87 and 168; receipt/mod.rs:68-70; signing_window.rs:41-45; delegated_server_signer/mod.rs:213-216). Every refusal then calls `signed_rejection` with `ex.now` — the SAME instant — (receipt/mod.rs:118-153, receipt/audit_event.rs:62-70 and 104-112), and `signed_rejection` passes that same `now` into `SigningWindow::over` (receipt/artifact.rs:64-66). So `over`'s credential always satisfies `now < exp` on the production path, whatever the exchange's wall-clock duration, and a stalled backend or slow-read client changes nothing. `over` exists precisely so that a signer RETIRED between ANSWERABLE and a post-dispatch refusal does not degrade the one receipt that must state the backend may have acted into an unsigned body (artifact.rs:34-40, answering_commitment.rs:11-13, mod.rs:167-174); making it fallible on `now < exp` would reintroduce that defect for no gain. G2/THM-0063 are also honest as written: they claim the advertised validity is `min(now + ttl, exp)`, which `over` does own (signing_window.rs:52-60), and the module doc says `validity`, not `usability`. The residual R-SEAL point — that `over`'s caller, not the type, carries `now < exp` — is real but unreachable, and its only current exploit path is the test at request_stages.rs:256.

adjudication.rationale: The rule measures mode bits and group membership only, and nothing else in the crate compensates: `violation` takes `(mode, file_gid, process_gids)` (mcp-re-proxy/src/config_state/key_file_access.rs:61-89), `mode_is_insecure` takes a bare mode (key_file_access.rs:112-114), and a repo-wide search of mcp-re-proxy/src finds no `uid()`/`st_uid`/`geteuid` call anywhere — the sole caller passes `meta.permissions().mode()` and `meta.gid()` and never the owner (app.rs:167-168). Concrete chain: the proxy runs as uid 0 (the default for a container that has not set runAsNonRoot), an attacker with write access to the directory holding `--signing-key-seed` renames their own 0600 file into place; `violation` reaches `mode & 0o050 == 0 -> None` (key_file_access.rs:73-74) and accepts it; `FileKeySource::signing_key()` reads it at the next root issuance (key_source.rs:231-245), and the replica mints delegation credentials under the attacker's root key. The containing directory's posture is likewise never examined. Real but conditioned on directory write access, hence low.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Pass `meta.uid()` from `check_key_file_perms` into `violation` and refuse a key file whose owner is neither the process euid nor uid 0 — one added input and one added clause, with the existing pure-predicate tests extended by an owner case. The directory posture is a larger, separable follow-up.

adjudication.rationale: The facts hold and the plane is genuinely inconsistent with itself. `cached` maps a poisoned cache mutex to `Some(Err(Unavailable))` (trust_cache.rs:235-243), `std::sync::Mutex` poisoning is permanent and `BoundedTrustCache` never calls `into_inner`, so one panic while the lock is held turns every subsequent verification on that replica into `trust_resolver_unavailable` for the process lifetime, under both the bounded-cache and push tiers. The other two mutex owners in the same plane take the opposite position and say why: `trust_epoch::recover` recovers because 'treating poison as a failure instead drops an operator's revocation on the floor permanently and silently' (trust_epoch.rs:32-43), and `ReloadingTrustStore::snapshot` recovers because 'the request path must not panic because a writer paniced mid-swap' (reloading_trust.rs:113-121). Three owners, three policies, none stated as the plane's. The direction here is fail-closed and the guarded region only does HashMap operations and a `VerificationKey` clone, so it is a latent availability cliff rather than a trust hole. One concrete inaccuracy to fix with it: `clear`'s doc claims a poisoned lock leaves 'the bounded-T fallback still capping the exposure window' (:364-365) and `evict`'s says 'the next read fails closed via `cached`' (:328-329) — the second is right and the first is not, because in that state nothing is served at all.
adjudication.smallest_fix: State the trust plane's poisoning policy once, in `trust_cache`'s module doc, and make this type agree with it: the data behind the lock is a cache and is safe to read after a panic, so recover the guard the way `trust_epoch::recover` does rather than latching a permanent refusal no surface reports. Correct `clear`'s doc in the same change — a poisoned lock does not leave the bounded-T fallback capping anything.

adjudication.rationale: The mechanism is wrong because the injected issuer does not produce the credential's CLAIMS — it produces only the signature bytes. adjudication.rationale: The R-SEAL finding for this owner, and it holds at main. `AuditRecord` is `pub` with four `pub` fields and no constructor (mcp-re-proxy/src/audit_record/mod.rs:66-78); `AuditSubject::request`/`response` are `pub` (:100, :108); both types are re-exported from the crate root (lib.rs:327-328), as are `AuditSink` and `StderrAuditSink` (lib.rs:329, :332). The funnel `record_to` is `pub(crate)` (:183) — the only narrow thing in the chain, and per CLAUDE.md `pub(crate)` seals nothing against the consumers, which all live in this crate. A producer census of the five emitters shows every one currently passes a verifier-resolved actor (pre_admission/mod.rs:143 `actor_id: &str` from the admitted request, accepted.rs:69 and notification.rs:83 `ex.actor_id`), which is precisely the R-SEAL defect: delete the resolution step at any one of them and an attributed record is still constructible, so `actor_id`'s meaning is remembered at construction sites rather than owned by the value. The brief's theatre caveat does not apply — `AuditRecord` is CONSUMED through the `AuditSink` trait seam, never produced through it, so the `audit_record` module can be the sole legitimate producer and module privacy is a real lever here.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Make `AuditRecord`'s four fields private to `crate::audit_record` and construct it only inside that module, from `record_to`'s arguments; expose the reads embedder sinks need as named projections (`event()` already exists; add `actor()`, `status()`, `at_unix()`, `subject()`). Give `actor_id` a witness rather than an `Option<String>`: a proxy-local newtype whose only constructor takes `&mcp_re_http_profile::ResolvedActor` (block.rs:190-197), so `attributed` means resolved. Two consumers will break and both are the boundary detector, not an obstacle: `mcp-re-proxy/tests/integration_async/delegated_client_server_e2e_test.rs:738-742` and :770-777 read `record.actor_id` and rebuild an `AuditSubject` to compare — they must move to the projections, never be paid for by widening production visibility.

Trust is resolved by `claims.issuer_kid` alone: `verify_authorization_decision` calls `resolve_issuer(&claims.issuer_kid)` (mcp-re-http-profile/src/pdp_decision/verify.rs:95) over the map `capability.rs:69` builds from `TrustDocument::authorization_issuers`, and that method DISCARDS the enrolled signer — it collects `(e.key_id.clone(), e.key.clone())` at mcp-re-proxy/src/trust_document.rs:180-185, although each entry carries a `signer` field (trust_document.rs:74, :142) and `request_signers` does keep it (trust_document.rs:163-168). `claims.iss` is compared to nothing anywhere in verify.rs:74-134 or relation.rs:90-134; on `Permit` it goes straight into `GrantAttribution::new(claims.iss, ..)` (relation.rs:128-129) and reaches the audit line as `authz_authority` via `AuthorizedRequestFacts::audit_attribution` (posture.rs:77-86). Even with one authority, `iss` is an unconstrained string, so the field is a self-assertion. This contradicts the claims struct's own header — 'Every field earns its place by a refusal it makes possible. Nothing here is descriptive.' (claims.rs:123-126) — since `iss` makes no refusal possible.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Make `authorization_issuers` retain the enrolled signer — return `HashMap<String, (String, VerificationKey)>` or a small `EnrolledAuthority { signer, key }` — and have `PdpDecisionPolicy::resolve_authority` hand the evaluator the enrolled name alongside the key. Then either (a) refuse in `PdpDecisionEvaluator::decide` when `claims.iss != enrolled_signer` with a new `PdpRelationRefusal` arm, or (b) build `GrantAttribution` from the ENROLLED signer rather than from `claims.iss`. (a) is preferable: it keeps `iss` a claim that earns its place by the refusal it makes possible, matching claims.rs:123-126.

Second, the only way that thread can poison the mutex is to panic inside `current_label`'s critical section — a comparison, a store and a `format!` — and `supervise_delegated_rotation` (rotation.rs:75-93) wraps the ENTIRE `rotation_loop` in `catch_unwind` and converts any panic into `signer.retire_permanently()` plus `metrics().record_failure()` and a FATAL log, after which the thread returns and the loop does not run again. The 5R+T case is the recover-on-the-fifth pattern: a request during the tolerated stretch re-caches the removed key from the last-good snapshot for a further T, and the fifth read then succeeds, leaving the counter reset and the cached entry serving to its own deadline. With the cadence ceiling `R <= T` that layer A enforces (config_state/trust_revocation.rs:346-352), 5R exceeds R+T whenever 4R > T — e.g. R = T = 60 gives 300s against a printed 120s. The delivered behaviour is correct; the sentence is not.

adjudication.rationale: The ordering is real: `decide` awaits `self.source.current(&binding.admission_id)` at admission_enforcer.rs:121 before `check_admission` at :143, and `binding.admission_id` is an unvalidated `String` straight out of the signed body (mcp-re-http-profile/src/admission.rs:146), concatenated verbatim into the store key at admission_source.rs:88-90 and issued as a Redis `GET` at redis_admission_source.rs:152-155. Nothing bounds its length or charset: `HttpRequestEvidenceBlock::validate` bounds only the assertion JWS (block.rs:495-502), so the key is capped only by `max_body_bytes` = 16 MiB (mcp-re-proxy/src/tls.rs:143). Reachable failure: any caller the trust seam resolves can drive one multi-megabyte-key round trip against the shared revocation store per request, up to `max_in_flight_requests` = 256 per core, using an assertion that would have been refused locally for free. The ORACLE half is FALSE: `AdmissionNotCurrent`, `AdmissionAssertionInvalid` and `AdmissionStateUnavailable` all project to the same wire code `McpReError::ActorBindingFailed` (mcp-re-http-profile/src/error/core_projection.rs:92-98) and standing.rs:96 gives all of them status 403, so the two cases are not distinguishable on the wire. The region's stated freeness property (pre_admission/mod.rs:5-8) enumerates nonce, approval and backend — a store read violates none of them as written.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Bound the id where it becomes a store key: give `admission_key` (admission_source.rs:88) a length/charset precondition — or refuse an over-long or non-token `binding.admission_id` in `HttpRequestEvidenceBlock::validate` beside the existing `MAX_ADMISSION_ASSERTION_LEN` clause — so an unverified assertion cannot choose an unbounded Redis key. Reordering `check_admission` ahead of the lookup is the larger fix and is not required to close the amplification.

The link exists and is stated: the marker is named by `EvidenceDigest::of(serde_json::to_vec(&retained_request(request)))` (durability.rs:266-270) and the hop embeds that same `retained_request` value as its `request` field (retained_record.rs:88-99, :124-131), which `ReservationMarker` documents explicitly — 'the same token the marker is named by, and the same one a completed hop's request half hashes to' (reservation_marker.rs:38-41). notes: Undecided inside its packet; needs mcp-re-proxy/src/startup_plan.rs (`SigningPlan`) and mcp-re-http-profile's `CustodyConfig` — the only places the checked pair could be carried across the seam.

adjudication.rationale: The seal really does stop at the crate seam, and `SigningPlan` is not a second owner that closes it: `pub struct SigningPlan { pub custody: CustodyConfig, pub epoch: TrustEpochPlan }` (`mcp-re-proxy/src/startup_plan.rs:226-233`) has public fields, `TrustEpochPlan` is a public enum with public variants (`startup_plan.rs:159-171`), `startup_plan` is `pub mod` (`mcp-re-proxy/src/lib.rs:236`), and `build_delegated_signing` is `pub` (`delegated_wiring.rs:79`). `CustodyConfig`'s `ttl`/`overlap` are public `i64`s (`mcp-re-http-profile/src/custody/mod.rs:98-100`) and `DelegatedSigningCustody::new` is `pub` (`custody/mod.rs:162`). Reachable failure: a consumer of either crate builds `CustodyConfig { ttl: 31_536_000, overlap: 60, .. }` and calls `build_delegated_signing` -> `DelegatedRotor::rotate`; credentials mint with a one-year `exp` and nothing refuses, while the ceiling exists precisely because `exp` 'is exactly how long an exfiltrated delegated signing key stays verifiable' (`config_state/delegated_signing.rs:240-243`). With `overlap >= ttl`, `issuance_terms::rotation_due(exp, overlap, now)` (`custody/issuance_terms.rs:35-37`) is true from the instant of issue, so every `ensure_active` mints again and `wait_for_window` (`signing_plane/rotation.rs:136-146`) never parks — a continuous root/KMS mint loop. Nothing on the mint path re-checks `MAX_DELEGATED_TTL_SECS`: `issuance_terms::mintable` only tests representability (`issuance_terms.rs:53-57`). The module doc concedes the gap (`config_state/delegated_signing.rs:26-31`). Severity revised from high to medium because the shipped binary's own path does route through `classify_and_validate`.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Give `mcp_re_http_profile::CustodyConfig` a private `ttl`/`overlap` pair behind one constructor that enforces `0 < overlap < ttl <= MAX_DELEGATED_TTL_SECS` and projects `ttl()`/`overlap()`. That is the minimal change that makes the operational test pass: with it, deleting `ttl_violations` in `config_state/delegated_signing.rs` leaves no illegal pair constructible at the site that mints.

adjudication.rationale: The `fetch_max` monotonicity defect is real; the "caller-supplied `now`" premise is not. `now` is the host wall clock: app.rs:946 calls `proxy.handle(req, now_unix())` and `now_unix` is `SystemTime::now()` in mcp-re-proxy/src/clock.rs:36-41, carried as `Exchange.now` (http_profile_serve/mod.rs:462) into `decide` (pre_admission/standing.rs:91). No caller can move it. The unboundedness in the other direction IS reachable with no attacker: `record_authoritative_read` applies `fetch_max` (admission_enforcer.rs:172-175) so `last_authoritative_read` never decreases. State -> outcome: the host clock steps forward by D (bad container RTC at boot, NTP step); one successful read is recorded at `now + D`; the clock corrects; the authority then becomes unreachable; `degraded_window_exhausted` (admission_enforcer.rs:191-196) computes `now.saturating_sub(last)` which is negative, so it returns false for the whole of D — the replica serves on last-known state for D + P + skew instead of P + skew. The operator was told `allowed within P={bound_secs}s` (serving_capabilities.rs:352) and admission_enforcer.rs:49-56 states "degraded serving is bounded by P" as a true statement about the deployment. No test covers a forward-dated read; the only clock test moves it backwards (admission_enforcer.rs:256-261).
adjudication.smallest_fix: Take the window's clock from a source one sample cannot poison: record the last successful read as a monotonic `Instant`/`Duration` elapsed rather than a wall-clock `i64`, and compute `elapsed > P + skew`. If the wall clock must stay, refuse (do not record) a `now` more than one plausible step ahead of the current value, and add a test for a forward-dated read as the mirror of `an_out_of_order_read_does_not_rewind_the_window`.

adjudication.rationale: The mechanism holds exactly as described. `Clone for InMemoryReplayCache` on a poisoned source returns `max_entries: 0` with `seen: Mutex::new(BTreeMap::new())` — a fresh, unpoisoned mutex over an EMPTY map (mcp-re-core/src/replay.rs:270-277). The only thing that then refuses is `seen.len() >= self.max_entries` with both at 0 (replay.rs:371). `pub fn with_max_entries(mut self, max_entries: usize) -> Self` (replay.rs:309-312) takes `self` by value and overwrites the field on any inhabitant, so `poisoned.clone().with_max_entries(1_000)` is a fully functional cache holding none of the source's admitted nonces and reporting no error, while `a_clone_of_a_poisoned_cache_admits_nothing` (replay.rs:596) keeps passing. This is R-SEAL's shape: the safety property is a field value a public builder can set back, and the unsafe state (empty AND admitting) is a legal, indistinguishable inhabitant. Reachability is indirect — it needs an embedder that clones a poisoned cache and then resizes it — and the proxy keeps this cache off the serving path via `is_single_process_reference`, so low rather than the reviewer's implicit higher reading.
adjudication.smallest_fix: In `mcp-re-core/src/replay.rs`, represent the unreadable-source state structurally instead of numerically: a private field (or an enum over the seen-set) that `check_and_insert` refuses on regardless of `max_entries`, set by `Clone`'s poisoned arm and untouched by `with_max_entries`. Then a poisoned clone refuses whatever a later builder call says.

The body of `a_signature_window_that_cannot_be_computed_clamps_to_the_credential` (mcp-re-http-profile/src/custody/mod.rs:989-1000) is `let until = now.checked_add(T).map_or(exp, |u: i64| u.min(exp)); assert!(until <= exp, ..)` — a re-evaluation of the production expression at issuance_terms.rs:65 followed by an assertion about the copy. `signature_valid_until` is never called and `sign_response` is never called, so replacing the production body with `now + ttl` leaves this test green. The property is genuinely covered twice elsewhere: `every_term_fails_restrictively` calls `signature_valid_until(1_000, i64::MAX, 1_300)` and asserts `1_300` (issuance_terms.rs:109-115), and `the_signature_expiry_never_outlives_the_credential` drives it through `sign_response` and reads the emitted `;expires=` (mod.rs:723-776).
adjudication.smallest_fix: Delete `a_signature_window_that_cannot_be_computed_clamps_to_the_credential` from `mcp-re-http-profile/src/custody/mod.rs:986-1000`; the uncomputable case it is named for is already asserted against the production term by `every_term_fails_restrictively` in `mcp-re-http-profile/src/custody/issuance_terms.rs:109-115`. adjudication.rationale: The window is real and the residue is harmless; what is wrong is a stated property. `reserve` awaits the marker publication (durability.rs:273-277) and constructs the rescind-bearing value only afterwards (durability.rs:278-283), so a future cancelled at that await leaves a published `<digest>.reserved` with no value whose `Drop` would withdraw it. The admission permit is correctly released (the local `permit` binding drops), so the only cost is disk debt — and a reserved-stage marker is honest debt by construction: it asserts no execution and is enumerable through `stale_reservations` (durability.rs:369-380). The claim that is false is `ReservedBeforeDispatch`'s: 'a refusal, an early return, a panic and a cancelled request future all drop, and dropping is the rescind' (reserved_before_dispatch.rs:42-44) — a cancelled request future does not drop a value that does not exist yet. `stale_reservations`' own doc enumerates two causes for a stale marker (a full queue, a dead process) and this is a third.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Narrow the two docs to what holds: `ReservedBeforeDispatch` rescinds for every exit AFTER it exists, and a cancellation inside `reserve` is the third source of stale reserved-stage debt `stale_reservations` enumerates. If the property is wanted rather than the honest statement, the code fix is small too — take the rescind responsibility before the await (a guard holding the marker path and a sender clone, whose `Drop` queues a `Rescind`, upgraded into `ReservedBeforeDispatch` once the ack returns); the rescind is already NotFound-tolerant (durable_writer.rs:103-110), so an unpublished marker costs nothing.

adjudication.rationale: The composition root's reads are genuinely SEPARATE reads, which is what the module's defence (role_separation.rs:152-156) assumes away. `MaterializedSigningRoles::establish` runs inside `build_key_source` at mcp-re-proxy/src/app.rs:418-425; the root then re-reads the chain at app.rs:426-428 and the response public key at app.rs:513-515 — for `FileKeySource` each is a fresh `fs::read` (mcp-re-proxy/src/key_source.rs:220-222, 235, 264) and for a KMS response signer a fresh backend call. So a transient failure at the `establish` instant followed by success milliseconds later yields exactly the execution the comment says cannot exist: `roles_collapse` returns `false` through the `_` arm (role_separation.rs:110), `MaterializedSigningRoles` is minted, and both later reads succeed so the server starts. Concrete: an operator who used one Ed25519 keypair for both `--signing-key-seed` and the TLS leaf, plus one EACCES/EIO/ESTALE on the seed during `establish`, gets a serving deployment instead of the G6/THM-0073 refusal. `a_source_over_absent_material_materializes_on_either_side` (role_separation.rs:334-386) pins the permissive behaviour, so nothing turns red. THM-0073's scope text in verification/generated/theorem-index.md:966 carries the same too-strong argument and needs the same correction.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Make an unanswered role a third outcome rather than an arm of `false`: have `roles_collapse` return a three-valued verdict (Distinct / Collapsed / NotCompared) and have `establish` refuse `NotCompared` with a message naming which role did not answer — the composition root already fails on the very next read, so refusing here changes no legitimate deployment, and it makes possession of `MaterializedSigningRoles` mean the comparison actually ran. Update the 'Infallible, and why that is not fail-open' note and THM-0073's scope paragraph to match.

notes: Undecided inside its packet; needs ADR-MCPRE-063 `CertificateChainEvidence::interpret_identity` — whether it can return a source other than the one requested

adjudication.rationale: The authority cannot return a source other than the one requested, so there is nothing for the facade to cross-check. `interpret_certificate_identity` builds its result as `CertificatePeerIdentityEvidence::new(value, policy.selects())` — the source is derived from the POLICY, not from which projection answered, and the code says so in place: 'the interpreter cannot label a value with a field it did not read from' (communication_assurance/certificate_identity_interpreter.rs:74-77). The no-fallback law is structural above that: exactly ONE candidate is projected per policy and there is no loop or second candidate in scope (certificate_identity_interpreter.rs:48-67, documented at lines 10-23). `evidence.source().into()` at identity.rs:115 can therefore only be the requested field.

adjudication.rationale: Two authoritative statements about one security-relevant field, and they contradict. `ReplayInsert::now_unix`'s own doc reads 'The same vestigial `0` anchor as the sync contract — a backend that derives a server-side TTL reads its OWN clock and ignores this' (async_replay/mod.rs:92-94). Forty lines below, `AsyncReplayTier::check_and_insert`'s doc says '`now_unix` is the instant the VERIFIER used for this request ... Passing a constant here would silently disable that guard in the in-memory store, which is the DEFAULT one' (mod.rs:190-195), and it passes the caller's real reading (mod.rs:225). The default store consumes it as a real clock: `insert_locked` calls `refuse_stale_retain_until(retain_until, now_unix)` (in_memory.rs:124) and `local_refusals.rs:20-23` confirms 'The stale check is judged against the CALLER''s `now`'. The trait method `atomic_insert_if_absent` (mod.rs:113-126) says nothing about `now_unix`, so a backend author reads the field doc. One correction to the consequence: the two SHIPPING backends read their own clocks (async_etcd_store.rs:285, redis_store.rs:594-595) and the in-memory store is unreachable in a deployment, so a new implementor following the field doc would break a guard that governs no current deployment — a future-backend hazard, not a live one. Still medium, because the field doc is the contract a new backend is written against.
adjudication.smallest_fix: One statement per fact, in `mcp-re-proxy/src/async_replay/mod.rs`: rewrite `ReplayInsert::now_unix`'s doc to say what the tier actually passes (the verifier's reading, the same instant the freshness gate used) and move the implementor's obligation onto `AsyncAtomicReplayStore::atomic_insert_if_absent`, where a backend author reads it. Keep the vestigial-`0` language only on the sync `AtomicReplayStore` trait (shared_replay.rs:150-161), where it is true.

adjudication.rationale: Spending the completion before the write is attempted is load-bearing, not an oversight. `complete` takes it first (durability.rs:337-339) because the queue-capacity argument counts ONE job per permit: a completion that could be re-attempted would put a second job behind the same permit, which is exactly the post-execution capacity refusal the whole permit scheme exists to prevent — stated at dispatch_committed.rs:38-46 and asserted by `a_reservation_is_worth_exactly_one_completion` (durability.rs:949-992). The diagnostic conflation the finding describes is also unreachable on the serving path: `complete` is called at most once per exchange, from one of two mutually exclusive terminals (http_profile_serve/mod.rs:505-517 -> reply_assembly/accepted.rs:111-114), so `AlreadyCompleted` never reaches the 500 mapping at all. Nothing claims a retryable completion, so there is no claim to narrow either.

adjudication.rationale: True at main. `admission_key` formats `admission_id` verbatim into the shared-store key (admission_source/mod.rs:111-113) with the doc justifying the verbatim form on operator-legibility grounds — a good argument for not digesting it and none at all for not bounding it. The id arrives inside the request evidence block as `AdmissionBinding::admission_id`, a plain `String` (admission.rs:146), and `HttpRequestEvidenceBlock::validate` bounds the ASSERTION (`MAX_ADMISSION_ASSERTION_LEN`, block.rs:493-500) and imposes no length, charset or content rule on the binding beside it. `decide` then issues a GET on it per request (admission_enforcer/mod.rs:118) before anything is verified about it. Redis keys are binary-safe and redis-rs binds the key as a bulk-string argument, so there is no command injection; the costs are a per-request multi-megabyte GET against the store every replica needs for revocation, and a control-character id that defeats the very legibility the verbatim form exists for.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Give the admission id a stated shape where the evidence block is validated — in `HttpRequestEvidenceBlock::validate` beside the assertion-size clause — a bounded length and a printable charset, so the legibility argument and the resource bound are one rule and the store is only ever asked about well-formed names.

adjudication.rationale: The mechanism is exactly right and I confirmed it at main. `issuer_validity_refusal` exempts `facts.self_issued` from the window (evaluation.rs:153); `issuer_revocation_refusal` applies `.filter(CertificateCurrencyFacts::window_is_orderable)` to every certificate above the leaf with no exemption (evaluation.rs:175-176), so a presented self-issued certificate whose window is not orderable is admitted under `Ceiling(..)` and refused as `IssuerUnreadable` under `Revocation(..)`. What the reviewer missed is that the three-way application is DOCUMENTED as deliberate: x509_adapter.rs:39-43 says `window_is_orderable` is 'reported separately rather than folded into the parse, because the production semantics apply it to a peer's own leaf and to an issuer whose revocation standing is being read, and NOT to an issuer's validity check -- where a self-issued certificate is exempt from the window entirely'. So the code states the rule it implements; what over-claims is G12's parenthetical, which attaches '(self-issued exempt)' to 'issuer unreadable/outside-window' as though it covered both productions of `IssuerUnreadable`. The divergence is confined to a malformed certificate (notAfter <= notBefore), is fail-closed, and refusing is arguably the better of the two answers. The evidence half of the finding is correct and worth acting on: the exemption is exercised only under a ceiling policy (evaluation.rs:415 and :568), never under a revocation policy.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Narrow G12's wording so '(self-issued exempt)' is scoped to the validity pass, and add one sentence at `issuer_revocation_refusal` (evaluation.rs:164-173) saying that a certificate whose window is not orderable cannot have its revocation standing read, self-issued included. Pin it with one control in `per_request_revocation_tests`: a chain of [leaf, self-issued cert with an inverted window] under a revocation-only policy, asserting `IssuerUnreadable` -- which is what stops the two issuer passes drifting further apart.

adjudication.rationale: All three facts are dropped at main, and the code's own excuse for one of them is wrong. (1) `.map(|_| ())` at admission_enforcer/mod.rs:167 discards `VerifiedAdmission::degraded`. (2) The no-evidence `Optional` path returns `Ok(())` at :107 with nothing recorded, so 'admission was checked and passed' and 'the call declared none and this deployment tolerates that' leave the same trace. (3) `AdmissionSourceError::Unavailable { details }` is built at every source failure site and then dropped by `Err(_)` at :131, so an operator cannot separate a Redis outage from a poisoned in-memory lock at the point of the decision. Meanwhile `record_request_accepted` (pre_admission/mod.rs:130-149) carries the authorization facet and no admission facet. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the in-code justification at :159-166: ADR-MCPS-035 §3 freezes `SUCCESS_EVENT_TYPES` — the `event_type` token — not the record's fields (mcp-re-core/src/audit.rs:67-71). `AuditSubject::Request` already carries a per-authority facet alongside the frozen event (audit_record/mod.rs:82-104), which is exactly the shape ADR-MCPRE-066 introduced for authorization. An admission facet on the existing `mcp-re.request.accepted` mints no third success event, so this is internally fixable without an ADR, and the comment claiming otherwise is itself an overstatement.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Give `AuditSubject::Request` a required `admission: AdmissionFacet` beside `authorization`, with the three states the decision actually has — NotEnforced / Confirmed / Degraded — produced by `AdmissionEnforcer::decide` returning a named outcome instead of `()`. The `event_type` allowlist is untouched. The dropped `AdmissionSourceError::details` belongs on the refusal path, not in the accepted record.

I re-derived the swap by hand over every negative test in delegation/mod.rs::tests: each mutates exactly one field over an otherwise well-formed, correctly root-signed credential, so `wrong_alg` (323), `wrong_typ` (335), `unknown_issuer_is_untrusted` (359), `expired_and_not_yet_valid` (373), all four scope tests (442-491), the epoch test (494) and both revocation tests (514, 526) return the identical verdict whichever order the four calls are in. `bad_root_signature_is_credential_invalid` (mod.rs:347-356) mints with an untrusted root but supplies GOOD claims, so a verifier that ran the cheap checks first would still reach the signature check and still answer `DelegationCredentialInvalid`. The one credential that would discriminate — invalid under BOTH the root signature and a later step, asserting the signature's verdict — does not exist anywhere in the crate. The contract's `code-reading-only` label for G8 is honest, so this is a missing control rather than an overstated claim; the reviewer's refusal-token-oracle story is a consequence of a hypothetical future reorder, not of main, which is why I revise the severity down.
adjudication.smallest_fix: One control in `mcp-re-http-profile/src/delegation/mod.rs::tests`: mint a credential with an untrusted root AND an out-of-scope `mcp_re_audience_hash` (or a stale `trust_epoch`), and assert the verdict is `DelegationCredentialInvalid` rather than `DelegationAudienceMismatch` / `DelegationTrustEpochStale`. That single case fails if any of the three later checks is hoisted above `check_root_signature`.

adjudication.rationale: `ExchangeProgress` derives `Clone, Copy` (exchange_state.rs:554) while its own doc at :700-702 claims the latch "makes monotonicity a property of the TYPE rather than of the current call sites", and G2/THM-0044 are stated over the type. With `Copy` that quantifier is false: a helper taking `ExchangeProgress` by value silently receives a snapshot, every `observe_*`/`latch` it performs is discarded, and the caller's copy then reports a strictly weaker consequence — with no warning and no compile error. I verified the finding's latency claim independently: every parameter in the serving subtree is `&`/`&mut` (mod.rs:394, :411; pre_admission/mod.rs:67, :94; answering_commitment.rs:98, :144; dispatch_commitment.rs:77; inner_plane.rs:109, :158; reply_assembly/mod.rs:60, :91, :125; notification.rs:115; accepted.rs:43), so this is latent, not live. This is exactly the quantifier defect CLAUDE.md's R-SEAL section describes: "this constructor checks X" quantifies over one site, "every inhabitant satisfies X" quantifies over the type, and only the second is a theorem.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Drop `Copy` (and `Clone`) from the `derive` on `ExchangeProgress` and change the five read-only projections that currently take `self` by value — `state`, `retry_semantics`, `invariant_violation` and the `#[cfg(test)]` readers — to take `&self`. A by-value parameter then becomes a move and a discarded observation becomes a borrow-checker error at the caller.

adjudication.rationale: The smell is real; the fix site the reviewer names is theatre. `ReplayKey`'s five fields are `pub` with no constructor (mcp-re-core/src/replay.rs:111-131) and the tier charges `key.principal` verbatim (async_replay/mod.rs:210, 224) while keying on `key.signer/audience/nonce` (mod.rs:201). But `ReplayKey` lives in `mcp-re-core` and its ONLY production producer is `HttpReplayKey::to_core_replay_key` in a DIFFERENT crate (mcp-re-http-profile/src/replay.rs:113-121; the sole consumer is http_profile_dispatch.rs:165). Module privacy in `mcp-re-core` therefore cannot reach that producer: it would force a public constructor taking the same five strings with the same absence of checking, and core cannot perform the derivation because the keyid boundary is a profile fact and core is deliberately profile-agnostic and pure (replay.rs:103-110). That is exactly the case CLAUDE.md calls privacy theatre. The invariant's real owner is one field higher up: `HttpReplayKey.actor_id` is a raw `String` (http-profile/src/replay.rs:41), and both invariants this owner rests on are functions of it — `principal_slot`'s `rsplit_once(':')` lands on the keyid boundary only because `ActorIdentity::field_escape` escapes ':' (block.rs:87-96), and `signer_slot`'s U+001F join is injective only because the same function escapes U+001F. The other four components are a compile-time constant (`PROFILE_TAG`, verify/floor/request.rs:136), a constant label, a base64url hash, and a slot that `composite_replay_key` length-prefixes anyway (shared_replay.rs:115-126). So exactly one component is unowned, and it is the one all the reasoning depends on. Note #885 (97e6b8db) already added `the_principal_slot_is_the_subject_without_its_keyid` and the injectivity control, so the derivation is test-owned even though it is not type-owned — severity revised from medium to low.
adjudication.smallest_fix: In `mcp-re-http-profile/src/replay.rs`: make `HttpReplayKey`'s fields private to that module and give it a constructor that takes `&ResolvedActor` (calling `actor_id()` inside) rather than an `actor_id: String`, with `profile_id`/`signature_label` supplied from the `ids` constants. That makes the keyid boundary and the separator-freedom properties of every inhabitant instead of properties of `prepare_http_dispatch`. Do NOT touch `mcp-re-core::ReplayKey`: privatising it there only relocates the same unchecked five arguments.

adjudication.rationale: The overstatement is real and it survives into the published index. THM-0048's statement clause reads '...a rebuild with withdrawn trust advances the epoch and stops resumption' and its scope section says only that the terms travel together and the epoch tracks the anchors — `verification/generated/theorem-index.md:687-697` renders exactly that, with no lifecycle disclaimer. The owner's own module table is explicit that proposition 2, 'a production listener's epoch advances when its anchors change', is established by NOTHING (`tls_listener_state/mod.rs:26-34`), and the code agrees: `bind_resumption` hands `republish` the epoch the store already holds (:218-221), so `SharedTlsAuthEpoch::store` returns `None` and the change branch never fires in a listener (`auth_epoch.rs:155-166`). The registered evidence for that clause is `auth_epoch::tests::a_rebuild_with_withdrawn_trust_advances_the_epoch_and_stops_resumption` (`auth_epoch.rs:399-407`), which calls `EpochBoundSessionStore::republish` directly — a store-level capability, and it is in `tested_symbols` for `proxy.tls_listener_state` (`verification/policy/verification.toml:543`). Two corrections to the reviewer: THM-0103's own scope DOES carry the disclaimer ('this theorem must never be read as establishing that a production listener's epoch ADVANCES'), and THM-0048's security consequence ('a withdrawn trust anchor cannot be survived by a resumed session') is nonetheless TRUE under model A — carried by cache non-continuity, proposition 3, `a_different_anchor_set_is_a_different_state_with_its_own_empty_cache`. So the defect is confined to THM-0048's statement and scope text, which is the one place a reader meets the claim without THM-0103's caveat. Severity high -> medium.
adjudication.smallest_fix: In `verification/policy/theorems.toml`, bound THM-0048's statement to what its evidence reaches: say the STORE republishes and stops resumption on a changed epoch, and move the listener-lifecycle sentence into THM-0048's scope as the explicitly unproved operational obligation (anchor change = new listener = empty store; rotation is by restart), mirroring the disclaimer THM-0103's scope already carries.

adjudication.rationale: The ratchet is real; the reviewer's 'caller-supplied clock' framing is not. `DegradedWindow::record_read` is `fetch_max(now)` (admission_enforcer/degraded_window.rs:49-51) and `exhausted` computes `now.saturating_sub(last)` (:65-69), so the base is monotone by design. `now` is the serving path's own wall clock — `now_unix()` read once per request in app.rs:949 and threaded through `handle` — not anything a caller supplies, so there is no remote reachability and the reviewer's 'if any caller ever derives now from something an attacker influences' is not a live path. What survives is the operational one: one forward step of T seconds (NTP step, VM resume, a wall-vs-monotonic mix-up) sets the base T into the future, `now - last` is then negative, never `> P + skew`, and the window reads as OPEN for the T seconds the real clock takes to catch up — during a store outage, which is when revocations cannot propagate. There is no plausibility clamp, no reset, and `DegradedWindow` exposes no projection, so nothing can observe or report it. The same forward step also expires assertions, which bounds the damage but does not remove it.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Measure the outage in `DegradedWindow` from a monotonic instant rather than from the wall clock: keep the last successful read as an `Instant`-derived offset so a wall-clock step cannot move the base, and add a projection so the posture/health line can report how long the authority has been unreachable. The wall clock stays where it belongs, on assertion and record freshness.

adjudication.rationale: Confirmed, and stronger than stated: the profile does not merely permit covering a credential header, it REQUIRES it. `require_conditional_coverage` refuses any request that carries an `authorization` or `dpop` header the signature does not cover (mcp-re-http-profile/src/verify/floor/components.rs:60-71), and `conditionally_covered_request_headers` names exactly those two plus the MCP transport headers (:75-81); the floor calls it on every request (mcp-re-http-profile/src/verify/floor/request.rs:94). The signature base is built as `"{identifier}: {value}"` per covered component (mcp-re-http-profile/src/sigbase.rs:296-299), so a covered `authorization` header puts its bearer token verbatim into the base. `record_open_leg` writes that base into the shared tier as `previous_request_base` (mcp-re-proxy/src/http_profile_serve/continuation/open_leg.rs:62-65) and the Redis store persists it base64url-encoded in plaintext under a plain `SET ... PX` (mcp-re-proxy/src/redis_continuation_store.rs:28-34, 84-90). So in any deployment whose clients present a bearer credential, a party with READ access to the `mcp-re:cont:` namespace recovers that credential for the entry TTL, and the module doc's "it holds public signature-base bytes (not secret)" (mcp-re-proxy/src/continuation_store/mod.rs:59-60) is false. adjudication.smallest_fix: Correct the claim and make the premise enforceable: replace "public signature-base bytes (not secret)" at mcp-re-proxy/src/continuation_store/mod.rs:59-60 with a statement that the retained base carries the VALUE of every covered component — `authorization` and `dpop` included, which §4.1 makes mandatory-if-present — and register that as a declared premise on the correlation tier with a named enforcer (a covered-component restriction, or confidentiality of the tier at rest).

adjudication.rationale: The arithmetic is as described and it is the CORRECT arithmetic; what is wrong is the sentence the operator reads. mcp-re-http-profile/src/pdp_decision/verify.rs:130 enforces `now.saturating_sub(iat) > max_decision_age.saturating_add(skew)`, and the same `skew` widens `[nbf, exp]` two lines up (:117-119) — which is right, because `iat` is on the ISSUER's clock and `now` is on the verifier's, so without the term a decision issued by a lagging issuer would be born partly stale. capability.rs:74-77 gives exactly that reason for reusing the deployment's single `--max-clock-skew`, and the widening is bounded: `VerifierPolicy::MAX_CLOCK_SKEW_BOUND = 300` (mcp-re-http-profile/src/policy.rs:113) is enforced at startup (app.rs:738-749), so the true cap is `--authz-max-decision-age-secs + at most 300s`, not an open window. The defect is that the ON line at capability.rs:60-69 advertises only the first term — 'decisions accepted up to {}s old' — and `PdpDecisionFreshness::max_decision_age`'s own doc at verify.rs:57-60 calls itself 'the verifier's own cap on how old a decision it will act on', which is short by up to the skew. adjudication.rationale: The conclusion is right and the mechanism is not. The Drop-borne rescind alone does not break the bound: it makes it exactly tight (one un-awaited rescind + one awaited job per permit = 2K, and a sync_channel of 2K accepts the 2K-th send). What actually breaks it is that the permit — the thing the whole argument counts — is released by a CANCELLED request future while that future's job is still in the queue. `reserve` holds the permit in a local (durability.rs:260-277): drop the future at the await and the permit returns while the job stays queued and un-acked. Same for `commit_to_dispatch` (durability.rs:306-317, which also queues the reservation's rescind on the way out) and for `complete`, whose job is orphaned while the caller still holds the permit-bearing `DispatchCommitted`. So a permit slot can account for three or more queued jobs, and repeated cancelled `reserve` attempts orphan a job each while handing the permit straight back — the queue can then fill to 2K with no bound from K at all, and `complete`'s `try_send` returns `Full` after the backend has run. Cancellation is reachable: hyper drops in-flight service futures when its connection future is dropped (async_serve/connection.rs:84-108). Severity medium, not high: the outcome is a 500 `EvidenceRetentionIndeterminate` with the `.pending` marker surviving (http_profile_serve/retention.rs:185-197), i.e. over-reported indeterminacy, not lost evidence, and it needs the writer thread to be thousands of jobs behind.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Make the permit outlive the job it admitted: have `WriteJob` carry the `Arc<AdmissionPermit>` (durable_job.rs:20-28), so a cancelled future cannot return a slot while its job is still queued and 'K permits bound the queue' becomes true of every job rather than of every job whose future ran to completion. Raising the capacity number instead would not fix it — repeated cancelled `reserve` attempts orphan jobs at a rate K does not bound.

Neither await is a queue-and-go: `EvidenceRetention::reserve` and `commit_to_dispatch` each `submit(..).await` a durable job and wait for the writer's acknowledgement (mcp-re-proxy/src/transparency/durability.rs:198-204, 238-242), which retention.rs:71-75 states includes the fsync. Concrete reachable outcome, retention enabled: with store acknowledgement latency L, every in-flight inner permit is occupied for L longer than the backend round trip, so the pool saturates at concurrency C where C·(D+2L) exceeds the bound and `prepare` returns `NotAdmitted` — a 503 shed for requests the backend could have served, plus a HalfOpen backend whose one trial slot is pinned for 2L, delaying breaker recovery. adjudication.smallest_fix: Keep the ordering, bound the wait: give `Retention::reserve` and `Retention::commit` an explicit deadline (they already fail closed on error, so a timeout is an existing refusal shape) so the inner permit's hold time has a ceiling that does not depend on store health. The larger fix — separating the capacity DECISION from capability ACQUISITION so the permit is taken at the crossing — changes what `prepare` means and should not be done as a bug fix.

adjudication.rationale: The mechanism verifies and the harm is reachable, though by a different route than the finding names. `answerable_stage` validates the credential at `ex.now` only (mcp-re-proxy/src/http_profile_serve/answering_commitment.rs:77, via `current(now)`'s `now < a.exp` at delegated_server_signer/mod.rs:214), the snapshot is carried across the backend round trip and signs both the reply and every later refusal receipt with `created = ex.now` and `expires = min(ex.now + sig_ttl, key.exp)` (receipt/mod.rs:97-111; signing_window.rs:52-59; artifact.rs:64-66). Nothing re-reads the wall clock, so the response's whole RFC 9421 freshness window is consumed by dispatch latency. The client's floor verifier refuses when `expires + skew <= now` (mcp-re-http-profile/src/verify/floor/params.rs:80-85). Concrete reachable failure: `sig_ttl_secs` is hard-coded to 300 at app.rs:725 and the default skew is 30 (VerifierPolicy::DEFAULT_MAX_CLOCK_SKEW, mcp-re-http-profile/src/policy.rs:108), while the inner-plane timeout is operator-set from `--read-timeout-secs` (app.rs:685-689). An operator who raises it past ~330s for long-running tool calls makes EVERY receipt for a call that outlasts the window fail the client's freshness check for a call that executed — the at-least-once hazard the ANSWERABLE stage exists to remove, relocated to 'stale at signing'. The second, narrower route is the one the finding describes: during a root-issuance outage the active credential runs down inside its 60s overlap (custody/issuance_terms.rs:36-38; overlap default 60, TTL 300), so `expires = key.exp` can be seconds away and any dispatch longer than that plus skew produces the same refusal. The ADR-MCPRE-052 §4 obligation quoted at signing_window.rs:4-8 is enforced against the frozen parameter, not against real time.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Make the credential's liveness a property of the window at the instant it is used: give `SigningWindow::over` a fallible form that refuses when `now >= key.exp` (which also closes R11-482), and base `created`/`expires` on a wall clock read at the signing boundary rather than on `ex.now`, refusing — not degrading to an unsigned error — when the credential has closed. A deployment-level complement: refuse at ANSWERABLE any credential whose remaining life is shorter than the inner-plane dispatch deadline plus skew, so the window cannot be outlived by the round trip it must cover.

adjudication.rationale: The ordering is described accurately but evaluated in only one direction. Inside `attempt_reload`'s closure the rebuilt config is produced first (`crl_reload_worker/mod.rs:148-150`), the new index is then published (:151-153), and `config_snapshot::reload_once` swaps the config when the closure returns — so a rebuild failure publishes nothing and the stated failure-atomicity rule holds. The reviewer did not evaluate the alternative: publishing the index AFTER the swap would mean new handshakes use the NEW verifier (refusing a newly revoked serial) while established connections are still checked against the OLD index (admitting it) — the permissive direction, on exactly the connections the per-request half exists to reach. The current order publishes the TIGHTENING half first, so the only disagreement it can produce is the handshake verifier being stricter than the index for a serial an operator has just UN-revoked. That is the fail-closed choice, and with two independent atomics (`SharedClientRevocation` and `ServerConfigSnapshot`) a genuinely joint swap is not available without a single value carrying both halves. adjudication.rationale: Confirmed, with the exploit bound tightened. The record is unauthenticated end to end: `encode` produces `<generation>:<status>` (redis_admission_source.rs:41-48), `publish` is a bare `SET` (:117-121), `current_state` a bare `GET` (:152-155), and `decode` accepts any well-formed pair (:66-78) with no signature, MAC, CAS or monotonicity check. `AuthoritativeAdmission::new` accepts any `u64` generation, and the R-SEAL test has nothing to delete because there is no check. The premise gap is real at current main: enumerating verification/policy/assumptions.toml shows NO assumption covering admission-store write authority (the only shared-store premises are ASM-0040/0041 for replay and ASM-0044 for the trust epoch), and THM-0004's scope explicitly disclaims it (verification/policy/theorems.toml:289-291). Reachable failure: an actor with write access to the instance — a co-tenant, a leaked credential, a compromised sidecar — issues `SET mcp-re:admission:<victim> 5:admitted`, and check_admission's currency arm (mcp-re-http-profile/src/admission.rs:443-461) accepts it as the authority's word. BOUND (from R11-506, and verified): the writer cannot admit an arbitrary workload, because the call must still carry an authority-signed assertion for the presenting actor at that same generation (admission.rs:406-441) and within N + skew (admission.rs:264-329). What a writer CAN do is reverse any revocation, or rewind a generation so a retained older assertion becomes current — for as long as the revoked workload holds an unexpired assertion. That bounded-but-total defeat of the revocation channel is why this is high rather than critical.
adjudication.smallest_fix: Cheapest closure that changes the security argument: register an ASM in verification/policy/assumptions.toml naming who may write `mcp-re:admission:*` (scoped to the admission unit and boundary.shared_state_store, with an owner and a review requirement), exactly as ASM-0040 does for the replay tier — the record's provenance then stops being an unstated premise. The structural fix is to have the authority sign `<admission_id>:<generation>:<status>` under the same root the assertions are signed under and have `decode` refuse an unverifiable record as a definitive negative (never as an outage), plus a CAS on publish so a generation can only advance.
